messages:
sarah: Heads up, ran into a bug in the async Python client when a 422/validation error comes back as JSON — the raised exception only has message/text and status_code, but the response body (validation details) is dropped. :eyes:

alex: Oof. Can you paste a small repro? which transport are you using (httpx/urllib3)?

sarah: Async httpx via our AsyncClient wrapper. Minimal repro: 
```py
async with client.chat.completions.create(... ) as resp:
    assert resp.status_code == 422
    data = await resp.json()  # contains {"errors": [{"loc": ["prompt"], "msg": "too long"}]}
    raise ApiError.from_response(resp)
```
When ApiError.from_response is used in async flow we end up with ApiError(str(resp.status_code)) and no .raw_body / .json available. The underlying httpx.Response is GC'd by the wrapper.

john: Hmm, I think the current ApiError only stores status_code, error_message and maybe headers. We never intended to drop the body entirely. Could be a streaming/iter_content path where we consumed then threw away.

alex: This explains some customer reports where they couldn't surface validation errors to their UI. We should preserve either .raw_body (bytes/str) + .parsed_json (if valid JSON) or at least .errors list when problem+ validation schema present.

sarah: Agreed. Proposal: ApiError should have these fields: status_code: int, message: str, headers: Dict[str,str] (keep limited), raw_body: Optional[str], json_body: Optional[dict], request_id: Optional[str] (from x-request-id). Make those part of the public exception surface and type them in stubs.

alex: For async backcompat, maybe add .raw_body and .json_body properties on ApiError and keep old .message. Add a factory method that takes either httpx.Response or requests.Response. Also ensure we don't attempt to re-read streaming body after it's been consumed.

sarah: Right — the fix in code is small: when building the exception, call await response.aread() / response.text if async, or response.content for sync, then close the response. Store the bytes. For large streaming responses we should cap stored bytes (e.g., 64k) and mark truncated.

john: Good point about truncation. Also, need to be careful about memory for many concurrent errors. Cap + flag is fine. 

devex-bot: Created issue #4621: "python sdk: preserve response body & parsed json on ApiError for async client" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4621 :robot_face:

ci-bot: FYI — I added a flaky test showing current behavior: tests/test_async_errors.py::test_validation_body_lost is failing on main.

alex: For retries: we should NOT retry 4xx validation errors. Make sure retry middleware checks the status_code before retrying. Also add instrumentation that records request_id header when exception raised.

sarah: I'll draft a quick patch: change ApiError ctor to accept raw_body bytes, json_body optional, and update exception typing in types.pyi. Also add a tiny integration test that spins up a test server returning 422 with JSON and asserts exception.json_body['errors'] preserved.

john: Can you also include guidance in changelog: "If you previously caught ApiError(str) and parsed message text, switch to e.raw_body or e.json_body". Add deprecation note for any old fields we remove.

alex: One more ask: when we parse Problem+JSON or OpenAPI validation (errors array), we should normalize into e.normalized_errors: List[str] for quick UI consumption. This can be populated lazily from json_body.

sarah: Will do. Action items: 1) PR to add raw_body/json_body + truncation (64k) + request_id capture, 2) tests for async+sync, 3) update types.pyi and changelog, 4) small migration note on SDK docs. Assigning myself. :+1:

devex-bot: Assigned issue #4621 to sarah, added label: "bug", milestone: "next-sdk-patch"

ci-bot: Test added to PR pipeline for validation body preservation.

alex: Thanks — once PR is up ping me, I'll review asap. :rocket:

sarah: Thanks all — sending PR in a bit.
